✓ Correct Answer: D — sits The sentence reads: 'Near the boundary between France and Switzerland _____ the interconnected superconducting magnet array, particle accelerator system, and helium-supplied tube network of the Large Hadron Collider.' This is an inverted sentence structure — the subject follows the verb. The subject is the list of components (the array, system, and network) — a compound subject but treated as a collective entity. 'Sits' is singular present tense, appropriate for describing the permanent location of the LHC.
 ✗ Why the other choices are wrong: A — is sitting: Present progressive. For a permanent location, simple present ('sits') is more appropriate than progressive ('is sitting' implies temporary). B — has sat: Present perfect implies a completed past action. The LHC is permanently located there. C — sit: Plural present. While there are multiple components, the sentence treats the entire apparatus as one entity (the LHC sits there).

Choice C is the best answer. The convention being tested is subject-verb agreement. In this inverted sentence the subject follows the verb: “the interconnected superconducting magnet array, particle accelerator system, and helium-supplied tube network of the Large Hadron Collider.” Three nouns joined by “and” form a compound (plural) subject, so the plural present-tense verb “sit” is required.

Choice A is incorrect because “is sitting” is singular and does not agree with the plural compound subject. Choice B is incorrect because “has sat” is singular and does not agree with the plural compound subject. Choice D is incorrect because “sits” is singular and does not agree with the plural compound subject.
